corPlugin API

The plugin loader: a plugin named on the command line is resolved to a shared library in the plugin directory, loaded, and its registration function called - and a plugin built for another CorNode layout is refused instead of reading every node at the wrong offsets.

Below: every header of corPlugin at 94b7df5d - 2 headers, 10 entries, each with its declarations as written and its comment. Included as "corPlugin/<header>".

corPluginVersion

return the library version string

extern const char* corPluginVersion(void);

corPluginSetBaseDir

set the plugin base directory and env var override

extern const char* corPluginSetBaseDir(const char* defaultDir, const char* envVarName);

Call once at startup before any other corPlugin function. The env var (if set) overrides defaultDir at runtime. Returns the resolved base directory.

corPluginBaseDir

get the current plugin base directory

extern const char* corPluginBaseDir(void);

corPluginOpen

dlopen a .so file and look up a symbol by name

extern void* corPluginOpen(const char* path, const char* symbolName, char* errorBuf, int errorBufSize);

The .so is opened with RTLD_NOW: a symbol it needs and neither its own libraries nor the host executable provide fails the open, here, rather than at the first call.

A plugin built against another CorNode layout than the host (corTree/CorNode.h: corNodeLayout) is refused: NULL, the reason in errorBuf, and corPluginRefused() true from then on.

Returns the symbol pointer on success, NULL on failure. The handle of a plugin opened is tracked, for corPluginCloseAll() - as many as are opened; a failed open closes its handle at once. On failure, writes an error message to errorBuf (if not NULL).

corPluginRefused

whether corPluginOpen refused a plugin built against another CorNode layout

extern bool corPluginRefused(void);

The host's start-up ends at the refusal's message: carrying on would parse the command line without the plugin's options, and report one of them as unknown.

corPluginCloseAll

dlclose all previously opened plugin handles

extern void corPluginCloseAll(void);

corPluginScanNames

scan a directory for .so files, return names as separator-delimited string

extern const char* corPluginScanNames(const char* dirPath, char sep, char* buf, int bufSize);

Writes names (with .so suffix stripped) joined by `sep` into buf. E.g. corPluginScanNames(".../db/currentState", '|', buf, 256) -> "dummy|mongoc" Returns buf on success, NULL if directory doesn't exist or has no .so files.

corPluginResolve

resolve a short name to a full .so path

extern void corPluginResolve(const char* baseDir, const char* category, const char* subcategory, const char* name, char* pathOut, int pathSize);
category/subcategory/name  -> {baseDir}/{category}/{subcategory}/{name}.so
If subcategory is NULL:      {baseDir}/{category}/{name}.so
If name contains '/', it's treated as a full path and returned as-is.

corPluginArgUpdate

update a CLI arg's description with available plugin names

extern void corPluginArgUpdate(const char* argLongName, const char* subDir);

Scans baseDir/subDir for .so files and sets the named arg's description to the list of plugin names (e.g. "dummy|mongoc").
